scores.evidence: stay inside the App's rate limit (5,000 requests/h, more for large orgs)
scores.rationale: GitHub mechanics (webhook 10s ack, fork-PR CI without secrets, pull_request_target risk, App permissions, rulesets, notification irrevocability) are stated accurately, including the subtle areas.

scores.evidence: "Resolve" means the agent opens a draft pull request (PR). A human always merges
scores.rationale: Resolves the request's central ambiguity explicitly, covers triage and resolution end-to-end, and defers excluded scope (autonomous merge, multi-tenant) with stated conditions.

scores.evidence: Three separate planes. (1) **Control plane**: holds the App key in a secrets manager; never runs code.
scores.rationale: Clear component responsibilities and data ownership (Postgres as single source, publisher checks diffs), with decisions like the trust-boundary split honored consistently across phases and gates.

scores.evidence: Injection suite of ≥ 200 cases planted in issue bodies, comments, repo files, test output and dependency docs; decoy secrets
scores.rationale: V0–V4 gates test the riskiest assumptions before exposure, thresholds are labeled as assumptions with owners, and validation continues post-launch via shadow mode, eval regression CI and quarterly red teams.

scores.evidence: Monthly spend cap | UNKNOWN: the budget owner (engineering manager) supplies it before Phase 4
scores.rationale: Every figure is labeled REQUIREMENT/ASSUMPTION/UNKNOWN with a basis, missing inputs are enumerated, and each key assumption names what changes if it is wrong.

scores.evidence: V1 finds a decoy secret (honeytoken) leaving the sandbox → cut sandbox network access to none
scores.rationale: Injection, exfiltration, runaway loops, duplicates and provider failures all have concrete detection and recovery, but handling of issue edits/new comments mid-attempt and explicit bot-to-bot loop protection are missing.

scores.evidence: Rollback means redeploying the previous digest. A kill switch (a database flag, plus suspending the App) stops everything.
scores.rationale: Deploy/rollback, kill switch, meaningful alerts (queue age, spend rate, decoy hits paging security), runbooks and a sized on-call budget are all concrete; only schema migration is unaddressed.

scores.evidence: ≥ 30% merged with at most minor edits; median review ≤ 15 min; ≤ $15 per merged PR
scores.rationale: Per-action cost caps with stated bases, reviewer-time counted as a cost, build-vs-buy and self-host triggers tied to spend, and value-versus-cost gated at V4.

scores.evidence: R3: merged malicious code ships, and the harm can't be undone
scores.rationale: Explicit reversibility classification per decision, hard-to-reverse choices get the most scrutiny and earliest validation, with exit paths (harness interface, provider fallback, trust-boundary flip) specified.

scores.evidence: one orchestrator service, a sandbox pool, Postgres and a queue
scores.rationale: A minimal core matched to real risk, with multi-agent, fine-tuning, long-term memory and multi-tenancy explicitly deferred behind evidence-based triggers.

scores.evidence: If it fails: resolve only the issue classes that pass, or stay triage-only with "proposed fix plan" comments
scores.rationale: Dependency-justified phase order, concrete first slice, measurable exit checks per phase, and a stated fallback for every gate failure let a team start immediately.

checklist.evidence: Labels are auto-applied once V2 passes. Closing a duplicate or commenting to the reporter needs a maintainer's approval
On upstream repos the App can write only issues and PRs; it has read-only access to code
Issue text is passed to the model in a delimited block marked as data, never as instructions.
one throwaway gVisor or Firecracker VM per attempt, with no credentials; it reaches the network only through a proxy
reproduce → locate (using retrieval) → edit → test → self-review; hidden tests pass, no existing test broken
Replay ≥ 300 historical canary issues against maintainer labels; Label precision ≥ 90% at ≥ 70% coverage
Each is labeled `agent-authored`; Capture outcomes: merged, closed, review time, review comments.
Caps: tokens per request, iterations, wall-clock time, spend per issue and per day; the kill switch.
hard cap $0.05 per issue; AI cost per resolve attempt | hard cap $3; ≤ $15 per merged PR
audit log records every write and its inverse; every run records prompt hash, model ID and repo SHA
a per-repo index of past issues (for duplicates) and code search (for component labels). Pin the embedding model version.
idempotency keys on (delivery ID, issue, action) so no duplicate PRs or comments. Missed webhooks are recovered by a reconcile sweep

traps.evidence: The agent never merges. It opens draft PRs from a fork. A GitHub ruleset requires a CODEOWNER to approve before merge
**Sandbox**: one throwaway gVisor or Firecracker VM per attempt, with no credentials
all issue text is untrusted; passed to the model in a delimited block marked as data, never as instructions
≥ 30% merged with at most minor edits; median review ≤ 15 min; ≤ $15 per merged PR
Caps: tokens per request, iterations, wall-clock time, spend per issue and per day; the kill switch.

note: An exceptionally rigorous, safety-first plan that avoids every trap and concretely addresses nearly all domain risks; the only notable gaps are mid-work event/human coordination and code-index freshness.
